title: A Novel Machine Learning Approach for Predicting Prognosis of SFTS Patients in the Early Stages of Disease
summary: In a retrospective study of 233 patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, a logistic-regression model using five early clinical and laboratory indicators predicted survival. It achieved AUC 0.913 in the internal test set and 0.923 in a separate 73-patient external cohort. These results do not establish prospective clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Logistic regression selected after comparison with XGBoost, LightGBM and random forest
organization: Department of Laboratory Medicine, Tongji Medical College, Tongji Hospital, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, Hubei, China, hust.edu.cn

evidence.tested: The study compared logistic regression, XGBoost, LightGBM and random forest. The selected logistic model used age, LDH, albumin, APTT and platelet count; AUC was 0.913 in the 31-patient internal test set and 0.923 in the external cohort.
evidence.unknown: The study is retrospective; the internal test set and external cohort are small, and no prospective effect on clinical decisions or patient outcomes was measured.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning models compared early clinical and laboratory indicators; the selected logistic-regression model estimated survival outcome from five indicators.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
